items.t: Wipers can stop working (recall)
items.note: Free under recall 98V-093 if not already done. Check your VIN with a Nissan dealer.

items.t: Misfire or rough running from spark plug wires
Check engine light for random misfire code P0300
items.job: Replace spark plugs and plug wires
items.note: Check first whether the Nissan bulletin applies to your VIN.

items.t: Water pump leaks coolant
items.job: Replace water pump and refill coolant

items.t: Alternator fails
Worn front ball joints
items.job: Replace front lower control arm with ball joint (one side)
items.note: YourMechanic estimates about $425 for one front ball joint on a 1996 1.6L.

items.t: Throttle position sensor out of adjustment
items.job: Adjust or replace throttle position sensor
items.note: Adjusting the existing sensor with Nissan's procedure costs much less than replacing it.

items.t: Automatic transmission slips or shifts harshly
items.job: Replace automatic transmission (new unit at a dealer)
items.note: KBB lists about $5,900–$6,300 at a dealer for a new transmission. If the fluid is old, a fluid change (about $185–$213, RepairPal) is the cheap first step; a used transmission costs less but has an unknown history.

items.t: Check engine light with transmission codes but no shifting problem
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $122–$179 for the diagnosis. Ask the shop to check the Nissan bulletins before replacing parts.

items.t: Timing chain rattle and front cover leaks
items.job: Replace timing chain tensioner, guides and front cover gasket
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $1,531–$2,161 for a 1996–1998 200SX because the front of the engine has to come apart.

items.t: Unstable idle and code P0505 from the idle air valve
items.note: YourMechanic averages about $192, but its 1995–1997 200SX quotes run about $509–$787. Cleaning the valve or fixing reversed wiring costs much less.

items.t: Check engine light for airflow sensor code P0100
items.note: RepairPal estimates about $363–$741 for 1996–1998. Have the connector checked first; it may not need a new sensor.

items.t: Check engine light for rear oxygen sensor or catalyst codes
items.note: YourMechanic's 1996–1998 quotes run about $339–$493. A new catalytic converter, if needed, costs more.

items.t: A/C high-pressure hose leaks (service campaign)
items.note: YourMechanic averages about $372 for A/C repair on the 200SX; its 1996–1998 quotes are about $556.

items.t: Airbag light on or airbags not working as expected
items.note: About $95–$100 to find the fault (YourMechanic). Parts such as a crash sensor or clock spring cost extra.

items.t: Worn engine mounts (service campaign)
items.note: YourMechanic averages about $673 ($267 parts, $406 labor). Ask a Nissan dealer first whether the campaign was done.

items.t: Dash and tail lights go dark
items.note: YourMechanic averages about $214 for this switch. Check the fuses and the dash dimmer switch first; owners say a new switch does not always fix it.

items.t: Torn CV axle boots
items.note: YourMechanic's 1996–1998 quotes run about $393–$607 per axle.

items.t: Radiator cooling fan stops working
items.note: YourMechanic averages about $164; its 1997–1998 quotes run about $281–$306. A bad relay or fuse costs less.

items.t: Oil leaks from the front and rear seals
items.note: YourMechanic quotes about $167–$241 for the front seal. An oil pan gasket on the 1.6L runs about $475–$493; a rear main seal costs much more because the transmission comes out.
